name: Burpee
description: The burpee is a full-body plyometric conditioning exercise that cycles through a squat, plank, push-up, squat, and vertical jump in a continuous sequence. It places simultaneous demands on the upper body, lower body, and core while elevating cardiovascular demand significantly, making it one of the highest-intensity bodyweight exercises. The burpee is widely used in metabolic conditioning, military fitness testing, and interval training protocols.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Adequate floor space needed.
steps: Step 1: From standing, squat down and place both hands on the floor.
Step 2: Jump or step both feet back to arrive in a push-up plank position.
Step 3: Perform one push-up — lower the chest to the floor and press back up.
Step 4: Jump or step both feet forward to return to a squat position.
Step 5: Explosively jump up with arms overhead, fully extending the body.
Step 6: Land softly and immediately repeat the sequence.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously throughout. Exhale on the push-up press and on the jump.
common_mistakes: Skipping the push-up — reduces the upper body demand
Not fully extending on the jump at the top
Landing with rigid legs — absorb through the knees and hips
safety_considerations: High cardiovascular and musculoskeletal demand — progress gradually in volume.
Not appropriate immediately post lower extremity injury.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range. Full hip and knee extension on the jump.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Performed for time (20–60 second intervals) or for reps (5–15). Pace sustainable throughout.
